fullPassage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.

questions.passage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

❌ ① 매개변수가 거의 없다: 본문은 'millions of ... adjustable parameters', 'a multitude of adjustable parameters'(매우 많다). 불일치

✅ ② 매개변수가 많으면 최적 설정 탐색에 오래 걸림: 'In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting'와 일치 ← 정답

❌ ③ 오류 신호를 완전히 무시: 'error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters'(오류 신호를 활용). 불일치

❌ ④ 감독자 없이 혼자: supervised learning은 정답을 아는 감독자를 전제. 불일치
det.tip: a multitude of adjustable parameters → it can take a long time. 매개변수가 많을수록 탐색이 오래 걸림.

ch: 신경망에는 조정 가능한 매개변수가 거의 없다.
조정 가능한 매개변수가 많은 공간에서는 최적의 설정을 찾는 데 오랜 시간이 걸릴 수 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 매 단계에서 오류를 조금씩 줄이며 점진적으로 나아간다 = 밑줄의 함축
det.analysis:
밑줄 'make only a small correction in the right direction(올바른 방향으로 작은 수정만 한다)'은, 한 번에 크게 바꾸지 않고 오류를 측정한 뒤 조금씩 올바른 방향으로 고쳐 나간다는 의미. 앞 문장 'I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it'과 연결된다.

❌ ① 한 번의 큰 수정으로 즉시 해결: 'only a small(작은 것만)'과 정반대

❌ ② 방향을 자주 바꾸다 길을 잃음: 'in the right direction(올바른 방향으로)'과 모순

✅ ③ 조금씩 줄이며 점진적으로 나아감: small correction을 여러 단계 반복 → 점진적 개선 ← 정답

❌ ④ 방향을 알 수 없어 포기: 'the right direction(올바른 방향)'을 안다는 서술과 반대
det.tip: a small correction + at each step + thousands of times = 조금씩 여러 번 = 점진적 개선. 그래서 학습이 느린 것.

ch: 한 번의 큰 수정으로 문제를 즉시 해결한다는 뜻이다.

올바른 방향을 전혀 알 수 없어 포기한다는 뜻이다.

다음 우리말을 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오. (영어로)
우리말: 나는 그것을 줄이기 위해 내 매개변수를 조정한다.
[조건] (1) adjust, I, it, my, parameters, reduce, to를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: I adjust my parameters(나는 내 매개변수를 조정한다) to reduce it(그것을 줄이기 위해)
det.analysis:
구문 분석: I(주어) + adjust(동사) + my parameters(목적어) + to reduce it(목적을 나타내는 to부정사구).

'to + 동사원형'은 '~하기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내며, it은 앞서 언급된 my error(내 오류)를 받는다.

단어 순서: I → adjust → my → parameters → to → reduce → it (7단어).
det.tip: to부정사(to reduce)=~하기 위해(목적). I adjust my parameters to reduce it = 그것을 줄이려고 매개변수를 조정한다.

[보기] activated, exactly, have, it, network, response, should, tell, the, We, which
(11단어, 영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 본문: 'We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated' = 우리는 신경망에 그것이 정확히 어떤 응답을 활성화했어야 했는지 말해 준다 (11단어)
det.analysis:
4형식 동사 tell + 간접목적어(the network) + 직접목적어(의문사절). 직접목적어는 'exactly which response it should have activated'로, 의문형용사 which가 response를 꾸며 명사절을 이끈다.

should have + 과거분사(activated) = '활성화했어야 했다'(과거에 대한 당위). 단어 순서: We → tell → the → network → exactly → which → response → it → should → have → activated (11단어).
det.tip: tell + 사람 + 의문사절(4형식). which response = 어떤 응답인지. should have p.p. = ~했어야 했다.

questions.passage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because __________ in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.

det.korean: error signals(오류 신호가) are sent back(되돌려 보내진다) into the network(신경망 안으로)
det.analysis:
수동태 구문: 주어 error signals는 '보내지는' 대상이므로 'be동사(are) + 과거분사(sent)'의 수동태로 쓴다. back은 '되돌려', into the network는 '신경망 안으로'라는 방향을 나타낸다.

단어 순서: error → signals → are → sent → back → into → the → network (8단어).
det.tip: be + 과거분사 = 수동태(~되다). are sent back into ~ = ~ 안으로 되돌려 보내지다.
